sayings.text: The knees are quiet. Enjoy the day.
The knees are behaving. Nobody make any sudden weather changes.
One out of ten. Nothing to complain about. A terrible inconvenience.
Today's got a little spring in it. So do I.
My knees haven't mentioned the weather once. Almost unsettling.
One out of ten. I'll have to find something else to complain about.
Not bad at all. I might take the long way to the kettle.
I heard one little creak. I'll let it off with a warning.
Two out of ten. I've complained about worse.
A good day to go out if you've got somewhere nice in mind.
The knees are behaving like respectable members of society.
Two out of ten. Barely enough trouble to mention over a cup of coffee.
A little creaky today, but I still fancy a walk.
Three out of ten. The knees have a minor objection. Overruled.
Three? Hardly worth making a fuss about.
A good day to putter about and see where you end up.
My knees gave a little creak at the front door. That's how Grandpa knew I'd left.
Three out of ten. I walked to Tim’s on sore knees. Grandpa drove and counted the walk from the car.
A little creaky, but there's still plenty of day left.
The knees started talking halfway upstairs. They could've waited till I had both hands free.
Four out of ten. Annoying, but not worth cancelling lunch.
These knees could use a slow start. I'll put the coffee on.
I can hear my knees on the stairs. Luckily, they're still quieter than Grandpa.
Four out of ten. Irritating, but not as much as the neighbour's kids.
A double-double first. Then we'll see what the knees have to say.
The knees waited till I sat down to remind me what I left upstairs.
Five out of ten. The knees have begun their commentary.
Five out of ten. I'll take the errands one at a time.
Standing up was fine. Sitting down again was even better.
Five out of ten. Not awful, just enough to be a proper nuisance.
Sensible shoes and sensible decisions today.
The knees had a word with me on the way upstairs. Then another on the way down.
Six out of ten. I'll supervise the shovelling through the window. Wave if you need more supervision.
Go gently today. There's no need to prove anything.
My knees noticed the pressure change. I wish they'd learned to send a text.
Six out of ten. I'll still go out. Wherever we're going had better have an elevator.
Take your time today. There's no prize for rushing.
The knees have stopped whispering and started making announcements.
My joints have gone on strike, and frankly, I support them.
A softer sort of day. Warm hands, a warm mug, easy does it.
Seven out of ten. If we can't park near the door, give me the keys and I'll wait here.
Seven out of ten. Any task involving the bottom cupboard has been cancelled.
Definitely a heating-pad sort of afternoon.
My knees have called their union rep. Even she said to leave a message after eight.
Eight out of ten. Everything downstairs can stay downstairs.
Be patient with yourself today. The world can wait a minute.
Eight out of ten. Even the Tim Hortons seems unnecessarily far away.
Eight out of ten. If you dropped it on the floor, congratulations. That's where it lives now.
Put the kettle on, love. I'm staying right here.
My knees have lodged a formal complaint.
Nine out of ten. Pass the hot water bottle. Yes, the big one.
Today calls for warmth, patience and taking good care of yourself.
Nine out of ten. I'm accepting applications for someone to bring me things.
Nine out of ten. If it requires bending, climbing or enthusiasm, it can reschedule.
Get comfortable, love. Ask somebody else to do the fetching.
I had three things on the list today. I've crossed off two and underlined 'sit down.'
Ten out of ten. I have officially run out of polite words.
Easy today, love. Tomorrow can look after itself.
Ten out of ten. I've decided everything important is within arm's reach.
Ten out of ten. Bring me a double-double and my good blanket. Then you can tell me what you wanted.
The knees feel good enough to shovel. I'm keeping that between me and the curtains.
The joints are quiet enough to enjoy the small victories.
My knees are quiet. You'd think I'd enjoy it, but now I can hear Grandpa chewing.
One out of ten. That's the nicest thing my knees have had to say all week.
The knees have reviewed the weather and declined to comment.
Standard says one. Personalized says one. Finally, a committee with no argument.
Standard says one; personalized says two. Someone has been listening to the knees.
One out of ten. I might go for a second walk just to make the neighbours think the first one was easy.
The knees are fine. Do not make a ceremony of it.
I feel good enough to share the cookies. I said good enough. I haven't actually offered.
Two out of ten. Plenty of room for tea and a little wandering.
A gentle day, provided nobody turns it into a project involving Canadian Tire.
The knees are cooperating. I shall reward them with very modest expectations.
The knees only complained once. If Grandpa asks, tell him that's the target.
One creak on the stairs. Between us, I think they just wanted attention.
Standard says two; personalized says two. We are all pretending this was planned.
Standard says two, personalized says three. My knees always add a little for themselves.
Two out of ten. Barely worth a formal complaint, so here I am.
I feel good enough to run errands. Keep that to yourself or they'll give me their lists.
Good enough for errands, as long as errands understand the schedule.
Three out of ten. A little creak does not cancel a good day.
Take the scenic route, provided it has somewhere to sit.
Three out of ten. The knees are coming along for the walk. They've asked about benches.
Three out of ten. We have survived worse.
My knees warmed up halfway through the walk. They could've told me before I wore the ugly shoes.
Standard says three; personalized says three. A rare moment of administrative peace.
Standard says three, personalized says four. Apparently I get the family rate on creaking.
Three out of ten. I have had more difficult conversations with a jar lid.
The joints are making suggestions, not issuing orders. Yet.
A manageable day. Do not ruin it by volunteering for nonsense.
Four out of ten. Move kindly and leave the heroics to television.
A little stiff, but there is still plenty of good in the day.
Four out of ten. One knee creaked. The other waited a step and did it louder.
Four out of ten. I can do the stairs. I'd appreciate it if you'd stop remembering things upstairs.
I made it down the stairs without stopping. I did have a few words with the railing.
Standard says four; personalized says four. Even the fussy numbers agree.
Standard says four, personalized says five. My knees would like that extra point entered into the record.
Four out of ten. I'll still meet you for lunch. Save me a chair with arms.
If the task needs a deep squat, it can submit a written request.
I came in from the rain and wrung out my socks. Now I've got two reasons to put my feet up.
Five out of ten. Slow is still a perfectly respectable speed.
Halfway up the stairs seems like a perfectly good place to admire the wallpaper.
Five out of ten. The knees are drafting a strongly worded memo.
I can do the groceries. Grandpa can do the part where they come out of the boot.
The air pressure shifted. My knees would like to know who gave it permission.
Standard says five; personalized says five. An astonishing lack of plot twist.
Standard says five, personalized says six. One more point and Grandpa's unloading the car.
Five out of ten. We are now accepting fewer unnecessary activities.
The knees are offering feedback. It is not especially constructive.
Tea first. Ambition can wait in the hallway.
Six out of ten. Be gentle with the machinery today.
There is no prize for making a hard day harder. Not even playoff tickets.
The knees had their say on the stairs. I made sure the whole house heard mine.
Six out of ten. I made it to the shops and back. Getting out of the car is a separate appointment.
My knees are sore enough that I checked the forecast twice. Still no apology.
Standard says six; personalized says six. Nobody is happy, but at least we agree.
Standard says six, personalized says seven. Either way, I'm taking the elevator.
Six out of ten. I can do it, but I reserve the right to narrate the inconvenience.
If it involves stairs, it had better come with a compelling argument.
Today is sponsored by sensible shoes and selective enthusiasm.
Seven out of ten. Protect your energy like it is the last butter tart.
A quiet day is not a failed day. It is a day with standards.
I took one look at the basement stairs and remembered we have a perfectly good freezer upstairs.
Seven out of ten. Even the porch chair looks like a sensible destination.
I brought the empty laundry basket down. If you were hoping for clothes in it, go get them.
Standard says seven; personalized says seven. At least the bureaucracy is efficient.
Standard says seven, personalized says eight. Either number gets you sent to the basement for me.
Seven out of ten. The bottom shelf can mind its own business.
I have one good bend left. It is not available for casual use.
If it cannot be done sitting down, it can wait for a better audience.
Eight out of ten. Comfort is a plan, not a consolation prize.
Put the warm blanket over my knees, love. Stay for a cup if you've got a minute.
The knees have filed paperwork. I assume it is a complaint.
Eight out of ten. The Tim Hortons is now a long-distance relationship.
I stood up to get the kettle. Forgot the kettle. Remembered every step back.
Standard says eight. Personalized says eight. There's your second opinion.
Standard says eight, personalized says nine. Either way, could you bring the tea to me?
Eight out of ten. Anything on the floor is now part of the floor.
Today's itinerary: chair, tea, and declining invitations with grace.
If the task begins with 'just bend down,' it is already lying.
Nine out of ten. Be kind to yourself and impress nobody.
Warmth, patience, and the shortest route to the sofa.
My knees gave a speech on the way to the kettle. By the time they finished, I'd forgotten what I got up for.
Nine out of ten. The chair has been promoted to essential infrastructure.
If you're coming over, let yourself in. You'll see why the door's unlocked when I try to get up.
Standard says nine; personalized says nine. Even the numbers have given up arguing.
Standard says nine; personalized says ten. The personal model has found the final straw.
Nine out of ten. Fetch it yourself, or discover how badly you wanted it.
Anything requiring enthusiasm has been moved to a later century.
The knees are not taking requests. Please consult the blanket.
Ten out of ten. Get comfortable and let someone bring you what you need.
Keep everything you need close. The rest can wait politely.
My knees have declared today a write-off. If anybody needs a second opinion, try the other knee.
Ten out of ten. I dropped the remote. Apparently we're watching the credits.
Ten out of ten and bitter cold outside. Put the hockey on. I'll let somebody else fall on the ice.
Standard says ten; personalized says ten. At last, a unanimous disaster.
Standard says ten, personalized says nine. I'll take the smaller number and the bigger blanket.
Ten out of ten. If it is not within reach, it is not essential.
Today has been cancelled by a very small but influential committee.
The knees have the final word. They are saying 'sit down.'
A fine little day, like a comedian who knows when to leave the stage.
The knees stayed quiet all the way down the stairs. I nearly went back up to check.
I went for a walk and forgot to complain about my knees. Very unlike me.
One out of ten. Even the forecast has remembered its manners.
A good day for a stroll, a smile, and pretending the errands are optional.
One out of ten. Damn near pleasant.
The knees are fine, which is bloody suspicious.
Nothing hurts enough to justify the performance. Tragic.
The weather has behaved. I suppose hell does freeze over occasionally.
If this is a trap, it is a very comfortable one.
My knees gave me the day off. Shame the rest of the family didn't get the memo.
The joints are cooperating. Don't get cocky, sunshine.
A quiet day. The knees have apparently run out of gossip.
One out of ten and still I find something to complain about. Talent.
I stood up without a sound. Grandpa still grunted on my behalf.
Lovely day. I hate how little material it gives me.
I feel so good I could shovel the neighbour's driveway. Idiot thought. It's gone now.
One out of ten. I got up without a grunt. So who the hell did Grandpa just tell to take it easy?
The joints are behaving like they expect a medal.
No drama today. What a bloody inconvenience.
One out of ten. My knees feel great, and I'm going to bring it up exactly as often as you wished I'd stop complaining.
I got up without saying 'shit.' Grandpa thought I'd gone out.
My knees are behaving for once. Nobody tell them this is what I expect every day.
I took the stairs and didn't swear once. Bloody waste of a good vocabulary.
Nothing hurts enough to complain about. Go on, then. Tell me what you did to my good frying pan.
Two out of ten. A little creak, then it's on with the day.
The knees chimed in once on the stairs. I told them I'd put it in the minutes.
A day for small errands and large cups of coffee.
The forecast has cleared the bar. The bar was on the floor.
Not every day needs a plot. This one can be a pleasant intermission.
Two out of ten. I made more noise opening the front door than walking through it.
The knees are fine. Don't make a bloody announcement.
Barely troublesome. I may have to invent a complaint.
Two out of ten. I've made bigger noises getting the lid off the peanut butter.
A little nuisance, nothing worth throwing a slipper over.
The knees sent a little twinge on the way out. I told them we'd already left.
The clouds are putting on a show. My knees gave them two out of ten and went back inside for a biscuit.
This day is so respectable it could host a church raffle.
Two out of ten. I have endured worse from a stubborn jam jar.
The atmosphere is trying to be dramatic. The knees are unimpressed.
If the day gets any nicer, I shall become unbearable.
My knees managed a single creak all morning. Pity the kitchen door couldn't show the same restraint.
Two out of ten. A damn near competent performance.
A little ache. I can save the long version for somebody who asks twice.
The knees are quiet. Everybody keep your bloody hands off the weather.
Two out of ten. I heard a creak. For once it might actually have been the damn floor.
The left knee piped up on the front step. I told it to save the good material for company.
I felt one twinge getting the post. I still had more to say about the gas bill.
A little stiff till I got moving. The dog and I both said 'fuck it' and took the long way home. I said it for the dog.
I barely noticed my knees today. Shame I can't say the same for whoever put the empty milk carton back.
Three out of ten. A little creak and I'm on my way.
The knees grumbled at the front step. They've been quiet since I gave them something to do.
A good day to putter around. I'll get to the rest when I get to it.
The knees needed a minute to warm up. So did the car.
Three out of ten leaves plenty of room for a treat.
Three out of ten. I have had more trouble opening a biscuit tin.
The knees are grumbling, but they are bloody amateurs at it.
I went up two steps before my knees had anything to say. They were probably saving their breath for the other twelve.
Three out of ten. A damn fine excuse for a slow morning.
If the joints want a meeting, they can book a room.
My knees creaked in the biscuit aisle. I'd have blamed the trolley, but I'd left it at the end.
A manageable day, which is another way of saying don't get clever.
Sun's out. My knees are up for a walk. The dog might have mentioned he's already been.
Three out of ten. Nothing to write home about, unless home has tea.
The knees are taking requests and rejecting anything athletic.
No heroics, no nonsense, no bloody surprise stairs.
A creak when I stood up and a sigh when I sat down. Between us, I supplied the sigh.
I walked the whole block. The knees complained once. Grandpa complained about the route twice.
Three out of ten. I can still get up without using both hands. Hold the applause.
I can handle this. I simply refuse to make it look easy.
Three out of ten. My knees and I are going for a walk. They can bitch about the hills when we get to them.
One creak getting up, two getting down. The chair's getting all the credit.
My knees grumbled through the first block. By the second, they'd bloody well caught up.
Three out of ten. I'll go to the garden centre. If you buy soil, you're carrying the damn bag.
The knees are talking again. So far it's the sort of shit you can nod through while you butter your toast.
Four out of ten. A little stiffness gives the day character.
The joints have entered their second act, with fewer stairs.
Take the day at a sensible pace and let the scenery do the work.
The knees were fine once I got moving. Getting moving was the part they objected to.
Four is manageable. Even the fussy days have a punchline.
Four out of ten. Irritating, but not worth flipping the table.
The pressure changed and my knees did a bloody drum roll. All I did was stand up.
The rain's picking a fight with my knees. It can come inside and help me get these damn boots off.
A four out of ten: the forecast's way of saying 'don't push it, genius.'
The knees are not broken; they are merely being difficult on purpose.
The pressure shifted and I creaked louder than the screen door. At least nobody tried to oil me.
Four out of ten. Enough to cancel nonsense, not lunch.
The forecast looked innocent enough. My knees would like to cross-examine it.
A little creak never stopped me. It has, however, slowed negotiations.
The joints have formed a committee. Naturally, there is no chair.
The stairs may kindly bugger off until after tea.
Four out of ten and already the knees want top billing.
I have survived family dinners with less atmosphere.
The knees started up halfway to the mailbox. I've had worse company on a walk.
It's grey out and the knees are touchy. If Grandpa asks how I am, tell him to pick one of those to fix.
Four out of ten. I'll come for a walk. If you say 'let's pick up the pace,' I'll point out you have bloody legs of your own.
I can still weed the garden. The ones in the back can consider today a fucking reprieve.
My knees have developed a small objection to stairs. The objection gets louder when I've left my glasses upstairs.
Four out of ten. I'm tying my shoes with one foot on a chair. I look ridiculous and I don't give a shit.
I can get things done today. Whoever put 'quick run to the shops' on the list can strike out 'quick' and bloody well drive.
Five out of ten. Middle of the road, with a bench nearby.
Five out of ten. I can finish the errands. Can the last one be buying myself a biscuit?
A slower pace is still a pace. The day is not going anywhere.
I can still do the laundry. Whoever put the machine in the basement can bring it back up.
Five means listen to yourself and save the grand finale.
Five out of ten. The joints have begun their damn commentary.
The weather can change its mind all it likes. My bloody knees hear about it every time.
Today is not awful. It is simply being a pain with excellent timing.
Five out of ten. I can do the shopping. I intend to lean on the trolley like I own it.
The kettle is a priority. Everything else can form a queue.
My knees have made their point. They could stop making it every time I stand up.
If it requires enthusiasm, put it on tomorrow's bloody list.
I sat down to tie my shoes and wound up having a cup of tea. The shoes can join me when they're ready.
Five out of ten. Enough to make me take the elevator and pretend I was going to anyway.
I put the washing on. Then I put a chair beside the dryer. Whoever calls that lazy can fold the bloody fitted sheet.
The weather can keep its surprises. I have enough character already.
The knees have asked for a smaller stage and a larger chair.
Tea first. Then we decide whether the day deserves our company.
Five out of ten. If you hear me sigh from the kitchen, I'm getting something out of the oven.
Halfway up the scale and halfway through the dishes. Guess which one I'm leaving in the sink.
Five out of ten. I can do the laundry or change the sheets. Pick one before I say fuck it and do neither.
My knees have complained every time I've stood up. I've started complaining every time Grandpa asks why I'm still sitting.
Halfway up the stairs I remembered I don't even like the damn sweater I was going up for.
I can get through the grocery shop. If you remember the eggs at the checkout, you're the one going back for them.
Five out of ten. I've come down with a mild case of the fuck-its. So far it only affects vacuuming.
Six out of ten. Be kind to the machinery; it is doing its best.
Six out of ten. The knees let me do the shopping. They objected when I remembered I'd bought stairs with the house.
Choose the easy route and call it excellent judgment.
The knees are sore enough to make me count the steps from the car to the door.
Six asks for patience, not perfection.
Six out of ten. The knees are making a damn persuasive case for sitting.
The pressure shifted and both knees kicked up a fuss. Nice of the bastards to agree on something.
If you're waiting for me on the stairs, sit down. I keep thinking of things I should've brought the first damn time.
Six out of ten. I'll go to the shop with you. Pick the one where we can park out front.
If there is no parking near the door, that errand is buggered.
Grandpa asked if I was coming upstairs. I said yes. I didn't say before supper.
A sensible shoe is worth ten foolish promises.
It's so damn muggy my shirt's stuck to the chair. For once the chair and my knees agree on where I ought to be.
No heroics today. We are not being paid enough for the sequel.
Six out of ten. Whatever's in the bottom cupboard had better be worth getting back up for.
The stairs can wait. They have been waiting for centuries, apparently.
My knees have become unpaid meteorologists with attitude.
I told Grandpa I needed a minute on the landing. He brought me the vacuum. The man's a slow learner.
Six out of ten. If I sit down with a groan, kindly give me a moment before you ask for anything.
If it takes two trips upstairs, it's staying down here till tomorrow.
Run back upstairs for your glasses? Yeah, right.
Six out of ten. I'll come to the shops if I can lean on the trolley. Get your own damn trolley.
I can carry the laundry basket or hold the railing. Guess which one is staying on the landing.
There's free parking two blocks away. At six out of ten, I'm paying the damn meter.
If you need me to kneel, have the decency to tell me how the fuck you plan to get me back up.
Six out of ten. I put the pie on the middle shelf. Anything I have to bend for can go straight to hell.
Seven out of ten. Rest is a perfectly respectable appointment.
I made it to the landing. That chair up there is beginning to look like good planning.
Keep warm, keep close to comfort, and let the world fetch itself.
The dog brought me his lead. I brought him a ball. We both know who's running today.
A quiet day can still have a very good punchline.
Seven out of ten. I made it down the stairs once. Who left the damn laundry upstairs?
The knees are not refusing work; they are negotiating bloody terms.
If it lives on the bottom shelf, it lives there now.
Seven out of ten: even the chair has started looking smug.
The day can take its ambitious little plans and reschedule them.
The wind blew the bin halfway down the street. At seven out of ten, that's the bin's new bloody address.
I have one good bend left, and it is not for your nonsense.
The joints are heckling every staircase in the building.
Seven out of ten. Fetch your own biscuits, you energetic fool.
I can hear thunder from here. The dog has claimed my spot on the sofa. He can bloody well budge over.
If the task starts with 'just,' it is probably a bloody trap.
Seven out of ten. If the sofa had a kettle, I'd be set.
The knees have unionized. Management is making tea.
I took the bottom step with one hand on the railing and the other on the wall. In my own house. Airport security should be this thorough.
The stairs can bugger off. Grandpa can bring the laundry down.
Seven out of ten and I've got a case of the fuck-its. The laundry can wait.
Seven out of ten. If you hear me say 'fuck' from the bathroom, bring me the bathmat. I'm trying to get my socks on.
I walked to the end of the driveway. The bins can stay there till somebody with better knees comes home.
Grandpa asked what I wanted for supper. I said anything he could get out of the damn oven himself.
Seven out of ten. I'd tell the stairs to go to hell, but I'd still have to go down them to get to the car.
Somebody dropped a twenty under the sofa. At seven out of ten it can sit there and earn bloody interest.
Eight out of ten. Comfort is the main event today.
The knees have submitted a formal request for fewer destinations.
Let the world be busy somewhere else for a while.
The kettle is now a long-distance challenge with no prize.
Take good care. The day can manage its own expectations.
Eight out of ten. The joints have made a damn compelling argument for blankets.
It's bloody hot. If you move the fan away from my chair again, you'd better be bringing me the whole damn lake.
Anything on the floor has entered a permanent relationship with the floor.
Eight out of ten: the chair has become a five-star resort.
If it requires a ladder, it requires another volunteer.
The knees are doing tragic theatre, and I paid for the front row.
Today has been placed on hold until further bloody notice.
It's raining hard enough to hear it through the windows. Between that and the knees, nobody's going to miss me swearing.
Eight out of ten. Ambition may kindly wait outside.
The joints have declared a small state of emergency, with tea.
If it is not within reach, it can bugger off until tomorrow.
I've spent so long on this chesterfield I've got a favourite dip in the cushion.
I'm saving my next trip across the room for something worth getting up for.
Eight out of ten: a grand day for sitting with purpose.
The knees say no. For once, I see their bloody point.
If the doorbell rings again, I'm yelling 'fuck off' from right here.
Eight out of ten. I made it to the kettle. If you want a second cup, put it in the first bloody cup now.
The doorbell rang. Whoever it is can wait. I only just sat the fuck down.
I dropped my glasses. The dog's looking straight at them. For all the treats I've paid him, he's bloody useless.
Eight out of ten. If somebody says they're just popping in, tell them to pop the kettle on while they're at it.
I got up for a biscuit and came back with the whole tin. Like hell I'm doing that twice.
Nine out of ten. Be gentle and let the day lower its voice.
My knees are giving a speech every time I get up. At this point I'm supplying the swear words.
Warmth, patience, and no need to impress the furniture.
The chair has been promoted to essential infrastructure.
Today is for care, not proving a point to a staircase.
Nine out of ten. The knees have reached their damn limit.
There's ice on the steps. I'm already at nine out of ten sitting still. Whoever wants the post can strap on their damn skates.
If it needs bending, climbing, or cheerfulness, fuck off.
Nine out of ten: even the rocking chair looks bloody ambitious.
Fetch it yourself, or discover how badly you wanted it.
The knees are delivering a monologue and refusing edits.
The day can take its heroic nonsense and file it elsewhere.
Nine out of ten and the remote has become a sacred object.
Just pop out? Love, it took me five minutes to get to the front door.
Nine out of ten. Grandpa said to put my feet up. Funny, I could've sworn that's what I've been asking him to help me do.
A nine out of ten. We are now accepting visitors bearing tea and closed mouths.
I can see the stairs from here. That's as far as our relationship goes today.
If it is urgent, it can come over here and explain itself.
My knees hurt sitting down. Imagine the review they gave standing up.
Nine out of ten. I have no fucking interest in your obstacle course.
Nine out of ten. The stairs can fuck off. So can whoever left my tea at the top.
Nine out of ten. If you want me to get up and see something, film the damn thing and bring it over.
Grandpa asked if I'd like to come along for the ride. I'd like to put my bloody socks on without an intermission.
Yes, I'm still wearing yesterday's pyjamas. If you feel strongly about it, you can bring me a clean fucking pair.
Nine out of ten. The tea's gone cold. Bring a fresh one before you tell me where the microwave is.
There are three steps to the porch. Today I hate every single fucking one of them by name.
Ten out of ten. Essential movement only, and kindness throughout.
The knees have closed the theatre and kept the ticket money.
Keep everything important close. The rest can wait its turn.
If it fell on the floor, say goodbye. I have enough trouble putting my feet on it.
Today asks for comfort, not courage. Courage is overrated.
Ten out of ten. The knees have made a damn executive decision.
Snow's piling up and my knees are at ten. Whoever asks me to go out can start by digging a bloody tunnel to the car.
If it is not within reach, it is not essential. Bloody simple.
Ten out of ten: the blanket is now senior management.
Everyone may keep their grand plans and shove them where the sun don't shine!
The joints have delivered the final punchline: sit down.
Today is cancelled. Fuck the schedule.
At ten out of ten, I can put on my slippers or I can answer the door. If you hear swearing and nothing else, I've picked the slippers.
Ten out of ten. Bring tea, or bring a better argument.
The sofa has won the election by a landslide.
If it involves stairs, it can get stuffed. That includes the clean pyjamas upstairs.
The knees are taking a curtain call and ignoring the encore.
Ten out of ten. All my polite words are upstairs. Guess where they're staying.
The final act is tea, blanket, and absolutely no sudden movements.
The day can wait. The knees have spoken, and they are not taking questions.
Ten out of ten. If anyone says 'walk it off,' they can fuck off in that direction.
Ten out of ten. You want to take my mind off my knees? Bring the good biscuits and keep your damn hands off them.
I dropped the remote. If this show turns out to be shit, I expect a full apology from whoever put it on.
At ten out of ten the answer is no. Go on, finish asking. I can say it again with swearing.
The phone's ringing in the kitchen. If it's important, they'll ring Grandpa. If it's Grandpa, he knows where the fuck I am.
Ten out of ten. I can hear you saying 'it's only two steps.' I can also hear you taking them for me. Off you go.

bonusSayings.text: The knees approve. Carry on.
Cooperative knees. Now there's a pleasant surprise.
The knees are quiet. Suspiciously quiet.
I asked the knees what they thought of the weather. They waited till I was carrying a full cup of tea to tell me.
Something's brewing. The knees have begun their commentary.
Some people check an app. I checked mine and then stood up. Only one of them called me an optimist.
The weather's got more nerve than a telemarketer at supper.
The spirit is willing. The knees would like to discuss the matter.
Something's got my knees talking. I'd prefer it if they took the afternoon off.
My knees are making noises that would get a car taken to the shop.
If you need me, leave a message with the heating pad.
My knees are sore enough to make the stairs a one-trip affair.
Today's a good day to be kind to yourself.
Even the rocking chair looks ambitious.
At this point, getting out of bed deserves hazard pay.
My knees are sore enough to complain without standing up. You can imagine the encore.
My knees have a few choice words for the forecast. The one I can repeat is 'again?'
I told my knees we had things to do. They requested a postponement.
It's cold enough that Grandpa asked where the heated blanket was. I told him he was looking at it.
Ten out of ten. Everything I need had better be on this floor.

wildcards.text: Take the day as it comes. The knees certainly are.
A warm mug fixes more than it has any right to.
Slow doesn't mean stopped.
There's no medal for doing everything today.
Listen to the knees. They've been around a while.
Be nice to yourself. Granny's orders.
Whatever gets done today is enough.
My knees have become surprisingly interested in meteorology.
The clouds are settling in. I've told my knees they don't have to give each one a personal greeting.
My knees were grumbling before breakfast. I told them to take a number behind the cat.
I checked the forecast. Then I consulted the senior forecasters.
Apparently my knees now offer same-day weather alerts.
The knees said rain. The window says sunshine. The dog says walk, and he's the only one with any follow-through.
I used to check the sky. Now I just stand up.
I heard my knees on the stairs. Unfortunately, so did everyone else.
The weather is free to change. I simply wish it would submit a request first.
The air pressure changed on {weekday}. My knees were kind enough to announce it before I'd got the kettle on.
The air pressure changed. I'd like to speak to whoever authorised it while I was on the stairs.
I bent down once today. That seems sufficient.
If you want it from the bottom shelf, you want it more than I do.
My get-up-and-go got up and left without me.
I'm not avoiding the stairs. We've reached a mutual understanding.
The weather may do as it pleases. So will I.
I'm conserving cartilage. Very environmentally responsible.
No, I haven't tried yoga. Thanks for asking for the eight-hundredth time.
If patience burned calories, I'd be an athlete.
I've got exactly one good bend left today, and I'm saving it for something important.
The knees are happy enough. Let's not give them anything to complain about.
A decent day for wandering about and seeing what happens.
A little creak never spoiled a perfectly good morning.
Nothing wrong with taking the day one cup of tea at a time.
A slower pace still gets you where you're going.
The knees are asking nicely. Best listen while they're still being polite.
Some days are for doing. Some days are for taking care.
Keep yourself warm and don't be in such a hurry.
Nothing wrong with a quiet day and a comfortable chair.
Today's job is looking after yourself. Everything else can wait.
The knees are off duty. Long may it last.
So far the knees and the weather are on speaking terms.
I checked the weather because my knees were loud. Then I realised Grandpa had left the morning news on again.
The forecast has satellites. I've got two knees and a lifetime of experience.
Something's changing outside. The knees have entered the chat.
No need to check the radar. Apparently I'm wearing one.
I checked the sky on the way to the shops. My knees waited until I was too far from the house to change my shoes.
My knees are forecasting with unreasonable confidence today.
Apparently sitting down is today's fastest-growing hobby.
Today's itinerary has been shortened considerably.
Lovely day. Almost annoyingly so.
Not much wrong today. Don't worry, I'm sure something will turn up.
The knees are grumbling, but frankly, so am I.
I can still do it. Whether I can be bothered is another matter.
If it's upstairs, I hope it's enjoying itself.
I've looked at the weather and decided it can sort itself out.
Today has entirely too much atmosphere.
If it can't be reached without bending, we don't need it that badly.
I have plans today. Mostly involving not making things worse.
If anybody needs me, they can come over here and make a convincing case.
The sun is out and I'm off to pull weeds. If I can't get up, I'll tell Grandpa I found a good spot to sit.
The garden needs weeding. I'm giving the weeds one more day to reconsider.
The garden can wait. It'll still be growing tomorrow.
I put those flowerpots on a bench so I could look after them standing up. Finally, some decent planning.
If that tomato wants picking, it can make its case from up there.
The weeds have won today. Don't let it go to their heads.
Even the dog thinks it's a good day for a walk.
The cat has been asleep for six hours. Finally, a sensible role model.
The dog wants a walk. We're currently negotiating distance.
The cat's saved me a spot on the sofa. Clever little thing.
The dog can chase his own ball today. He's got four good knees.
Good enough for a few errands. Might even stop somewhere nice.
I've got three errands and enough enthusiasm for roughly one and a half.
If the shop doesn't have parking near the door, we didn't need it anyway.
That errand has been officially promoted to tomorrow's problem.
Nice day out. Come on, Grandpa, let's go before we change our minds.
Grandpa says the weather looks fine. He's welcome to tell that to my knees.
Grandpa made the tea. I knew I kept him around for something.
Grandpa's doing the fetching today. He's thrilled. Probably.
Grandpa asked if I wanted to go out. I asked if he had reviewed the forecast.
Good day for a family visit. Put the kettle on and pass the butter tarts.
The family's coming over. I've hidden the good butter tarts accordingly.
The grandkids can come over. They keep me moving and laughing.
The grandkids have enough energy for all of us. Convenient, really.
Family's always welcome. Just don't expect me to fetch anything.
If the family wants dinner, they know where the kitchen is.
Lovely day for the family to visit me instead.
Not a bad day for a little shopping and a treat on the way home.
I've only got three things on the shopping list. We'll see how that turns out.
I went in for milk. Apparently we needed six other things.
We'll do the shopping slowly. The groceries aren't going anywhere.
If it's not on the shopping list, I'm not walking another aisle for it.
If we're going shopping, tell me which shops have somewhere to sit.
Shopping can wait. We've got bread, tea and no convincing reason to leave.
Good day to make something that leaves the kitchen smelling wonderful.
I'm cooking something easy tonight. That's what recipes are supposed to be for.
Something warm in the oven makes almost any day better.
Dinner tonight will be whatever requires the fewest trips across the kitchen.
If supper needs more than one pot, we're having something else.
Tonight's recipe is leftovers. Step one: heat them up. Step two: don't complain.
Feeling pretty good today. Might put on some music and actually get things done.
The knees are quiet. It's like finding a good song on the radio before the DJ talks over it.
The knees are behaving. Whatever. I'm not making a big deal about it.
The snow tyres are doing their job. Now if only they'd make a decent pair for my boots.
I went a whole block before I thought about my knees. Then I thought about a butter tart.
My knees feel fine. Don't jinx it.
Plenty of life left in these knees. Just don't ask them to rollerskate.
The knees are creaking. I've made louder noises looking for parking in December.
I've been ignoring minor inconveniences since before call display.
My knees are giving this weather two stars and no written review.
A little stiff today. Nothing worth cancelling the afternoon over.
My knees have more static than an AM radio under a bridge.
I've dealt with dial-up internet. I can deal with this.
The knees are buffering. Give them a minute.
Today's mood is somewhere between whatever and don't push it.
Take your time. The groceries will still be there after a coffee.
My knees just made a noise like a cassette being eaten by the tape deck.
I'd rewind this morning if it meant I could get out of bed a little more gently.
My knees sound like the garage band next door. All percussion.
We'll take it easy today. That's not quitting. That's pacing.
The knees are acting like somebody left them in the car overnight.
If this weather were a mixtape, I'd record over it.
My knees are making enough noise without an amplifier.
Coffee first. Decisions second. Knees somewhere after that.
It's raining. My knees would like me to know they put in a complaint before the first drop hit the window.
I stood up too fast and briefly saw the entire 1980s.
Getting off this sofa now requires a loading screen.
The air pressure moved and my knees started up. With that kind of timing they could at least tell me when the toast is done.
Nothing wrong with putting your feet up before dinner.
Remember when we could sit on the floor and just get back up? Good times.
I used to dance all night. Now I make a noise getting out of the car.
Grandpa says we're not that old. Grandpa also can't find his glasses.
Grandpa can drive. I'll control the radio. Everyone wins.
My knees just made the Windows shutdown sound, and I'm taking the hint.
Today's dress code is sweatpants and lowered expectations.
The spirit says concert. The knees say seated venue.
No, I don't want to go to the mall. I did my time.
If you need me, call the landline. I won't answer that either.
I survived shoulder pads. I can survive the stairs. Give me a minute between the two.
Cold enough for a toque indoors. Grandpa laughed until I told him I had another one.
Grandpa suggested a walk. I suggested he take the dog and bring me back a coffee.
Grandpa can get the groceries. He knows where we keep the car.
My knees have switched from FM to mostly static.
Today's plans have been returned to the video store without being watched.
Getting downstairs currently looks like a choose-your-own-adventure.
The cold front got here before my knees were out of bed. Awfully keen for something nobody invited.
Today's a good day for an old movie, a blanket, and nowhere else to be.
Put an old movie on. As long as nobody asks me to get up and change the tape.
I sent Grandpa to check the weather. He said it was fine. I've sent him back out to bring the bins in.
My knees are older than Google and considerably less interested in your search results.
Not much to report today. That's the way I like it.
Everything seems to be working. Let's not draw attention to it.
Feeling good today. Don't make it weird.
The knees are cooperating. I've decided not to ask why.
Good day to get a few things done and leave a few things undone.
The knees are fine. Let's quit while we're ahead.
It's suspiciously pleasant out. I'm keeping an eye on it.
A little movement, a little rest. Seems reasonable.
The knees have noticed something, but they're not escalating yet.
Nothing I can't handle. I've met Mondays.
One knee creaked coming down. The other waited until I told Grandpa I was fine.
Do what feels good today and leave some energy for tomorrow.
There's a bit of complaining in the lower half. Management is aware.
I'm fine. That's not an invitation for follow-up questions.
No need to rush. Nothing good ever came from putting your socks on angrily.
Apparently the atmosphere has opinions again.
I can do everything I planned today. I just don't see why I should.
My knees have detected nonsense in the atmosphere.
A decent day to lower the expectations and raise the comfort level.
The knees have requested fewer surprises today.
I'm functioning. Let's not get ambitious.
Standing up is currently a decision, not a reflex.
Today's energy level is somewhere between maybe and absolutely not.
If today needs to be slower, let it be slower.
I have plans. The knees have submitted amendments.
I wasn't procrastinating. I was waiting for my knees to approve the project.
Do the important things. The rest can mind its own business.
The floor seems further away than it did yesterday.
If it's not urgent, it's enjoying a lovely day on tomorrow's list.
I've reached the age where the weather gets the first word and the knees get the last three.
Someone asked if I wanted to go out. I admired their optimism.
Today doesn't need to be productive to be a good day.
I've started measuring distances by whether they're worth standing up for.
If you hear me say 'I'm fine' while standing up, give me a minute.
My knees are providing unsolicited feedback again.
I've lowered my standards for what counts as nearby.
Pick one thing worth doing today. The rest will keep.
The knees have switched to strongly worded body language.
I'm not cancelling. I'm aggressively rescheduling.
Today has a surprising number of things that can wait until tomorrow.
If I have to put proper shoes on, the answer is probably no.
You don't have to earn a quiet afternoon.
I've entered the part of the day where dropped objects belong to the floor.
If nobody's bleeding and nothing's on fire, it can wait.
Get comfortable. Today isn't asking for heroics.
I've reviewed today's agenda. Sitting features prominently.
I'm available today for things that require absolutely no crouching.
I dropped something earlier. We've both accepted the situation.
Some days you push through. Today, you put your feet up.
Today's capacity is one thing. Choose carefully.
Good day for seeing the family. Even better if someone else is hosting.
The family group chat is busy. I've chosen peace.
I love my family. That's why some of them have their own houses.
There's always room for family. Chairs, however, are first come, first served.
Someone in this family knows where my good scissors went.
Apparently everyone needs something today. How lovely for them.
The family can come over. Just give me ten minutes to become presentable.
The kids say they'll only stay an hour. That's adorable.
If everyone's coming over, somebody else is carrying the chairs.
The grandkids can visit. I'll supervise from a comfortable distance.
Family time sounds lovely. Make sure somebody brings dessert.
Yes, you can come over. No, I'm not cleaning first.
I've reached the age where quality family time includes someone carrying things for me.
If the family wants a big dinner, I've got excellent news about takeout.
Come visit, love. Just let yourself in.
The grandkids have offered to help. I'm documenting this historic occasion.
I raised children. I have nothing left to prove today.
I'll get something useful done while the knees are feeling good. Probably hide the jobs I don't want to do tomorrow.
I've made a list. That counts as making progress.
Another meeting? I'm sure this one will fix everything.
I've been working long enough to know that urgent and important are not the same thing.
One thing at a time. It'll all get done eventually.
The email said quick question. We both know how this ends.
If everything is a priority, nothing is.
I'll circle back as soon as I can stand up without the meeting hearing about it.
I'll circle back when I can get out of this chair without making a speech about it.
Do what's useful today. The busywork can wait.
I've attended enough meetings to know this could've been an email.
I'm happy to multitask. I'll ignore several things at once.
Today's productivity goal is to look convincingly unavailable.
Finish what matters and call it a day.
That's tomorrow's problem. Tomorrow can file a complaint.
I'm working smarter today. Mostly from this chair.
Today I'm delegating anything that involves stairs.
I put something somewhere safe. It's gone forever.
The laundry can wait until the coffee's finished.
Whoever finished the milk had one job.
I cleaned this room yesterday. Apparently nobody was impressed.
The password needs a capital, a number, a symbol and apparently a blood sample.
The fitted sheet and I have agreed to stop pretending we're friends.
I just sat down, so naturally everything I need is in the other room.
The package arrived. The thing I actually ordered is apparently coming separately.
I don't know who put that on the bottom shelf, but we're no longer speaking.
Nothing makes you reconsider your priorities like dropping a sock behind the dryer.
The phone's at two percent. Honestly, same.
The smoke alarm only needs a new battery at three in the morning. It's tradition.
I finally got comfortable, so of course someone's at the door.
Whatever rolled under the sofa belongs to the sofa now.
If the remote isn't within reach, we're watching whatever's already on.
